text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola). The combination of a generalized nonpruritic rash, high fever, and a seizure (likely a febrile seizure or status epilepticus associated with the infection), coupled with normal blood work which rules out severe bacterial sepsis, strongly points to a viral etiology, with Measles being the most common cause of this specific triad in unvaccinated populations.
